lead: >-
  Xunantunich is an ancient Maya city in western Belize, close to San Ignacio. Its stone plazas and El Castillo pyramid make it a natural stop on a journey through the Cayo District. Two current Ada Tours itineraries include the site on different eight-day routes: one combines inland Belize with San Pedro Island, while the other adds the ruins of Tikal in Guatemala. Compare the itineraries and their included excursions.

## Ada Tours itineraries visiting Xunantunich

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that include [Xunantunich](/belize/place/xunantunich/) on their **main itineraries**, rather than offering it only as an optional extra. Both combine mainland Belize with time on the Caribbean coast, but their other stops and transport arrangements differ significantly.

Xunantunich is in western Belize, Cayo District, near the village of San José Succotz. Visitors reach the archaeological site by crossing the Mopan River on a hand-operated ferry. The ancient plazas, buildings and tall temple complex of El Castillo have survived. The main pyramid rises approximately 40 m above the plaza.

This site is well suited to travelers who want to see Maya architecture on an organized journey while still making time for [San Ignacio](/belize/place/san-ignacio/), caves and Caribbean islands.

## "Mainland / Island": Maya ruins and adventures in Belize

On the [eight-day "Belize: Mainland / Island Adventure" tour](/belize/tour/belize-mainland-island-adventure/), Xunantunich is visited **on day 2**. In the morning, guests take a guided excursion to the [Belize Zoo](/belize/place/belize-zoo/) and the ancient ruins. **Lunch and admission tickets are included.** After the excursion, they travel to San Ignacio and spend the night at Cahal Pech Village.

Day 3 includes an excursion along the Panti medicinal trail and a visit to a butterfly farm. On day 4, the program features **cave tubing** on an underground river in the "Jaguar Paw" area, after which travelers fly to San Pedro. The following day is devoted to snorkeling in the [Hol Chan Marine Reserve](/belize/place/hol-chan-marine-reserve/) and Shark Ray Alley; the final part of the journey takes place on [Ambergris Caye](/belize/place/ambergris-caye/).

This option is for travelers who want to combine Maya sites with different outdoor activities: forest excursions, a cave float and snorkeling. **Tikal in Guatemala is not included in this tour.**

## "Best of Belize": Xunantunich and Tikal

On the ["Best of Belize" tour](/belize/tour/best-of-belize/), Xunantunich is visited **on day 3**. Before that, travelers begin their trip near [Lamanai](/belize/place/lamanai/), where the lodge program includes nature and cultural activities. The group then travels to [San Ignacio](/belize/place/san-ignacio/).

Day 3 is devoted to a guided excursion to the Xunantunich ruins en route to Cayo. A guide, lunch and entrance tickets are included. Afterward, travelers check in at Cahal Pech Village for two nights.

**On day 4, the journey continues to [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/) in Guatemala.** There is a guided excursion around the archaeological site, after which visitors return to San Ignacio. Tickets and lunch are included, while **border fees are paid separately**. The Guatemala leg is not simply another Belizean landmark: it involves crossing an international border.

Day 5 combines cave tubing and the Belize Zoo, then the group travels to the coast and takes a ferry to San Pedro. The final days are for relaxation and optional marine activities. This version is especially suitable for travelers who want to compare two major Maya cultural centers on one trip.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_beliz_priklyuchenie_materik_ostrov,tour_source_luchshee_v_belize}}

## Choosing between the two itineraries

| Criterion | Main difference |
|---|---|
| Xunantunich | Day 2 or day 3 |
| Other ruins | "Best of Belize" includes Tikal |
| Starting area | City or Lamanai |
| Journey to the sea | Domestic flight or ferry |
| Final destination | San Pedro Island |

**Choose "Mainland / Island"** if, besides Xunantunich, you want tropical forests, a butterfly farm and a domestic flight to the island. This itinerary emphasizes a variety of activities within Belize.

**Choose "Best of Belize"** if you want to add another celebrated ancient Maya city, [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/), to Xunantunich. The route extends beyond Belize and requires additional border arrangements.

Both tours include a guided visit to Xunantunich, admission tickets and lunch. Prices and other details of each option appear in the tour table above. Read the selected itinerary for optional services instead of applying one tour's terms to another.

## What you will see at Xunantunich

[Xunantunich](/belize/place/xunantunich/) is known for the monumental architecture of the ancient Maya. Its most prominent structure is **El Castillo**, a pyramid towering over the central plazas. Its façades retain imagery and architectural elements linked to ritual representations of the Maya Classic period. Other temples and palace structures also stand on the site.

Unlike an archaeological site completely hidden in dense jungle, the experience here centers on open plazas, stone stairways and views of the green Cayo hills. A guide can help explain the structures' functions and historical context. Both our tours include guiding at the site.

Both journeys visit the [San Ignacio](/belize/place/san-ignacio/) area, making Xunantunich part of a broader introduction to western Belize. For a closer comparison of heritage-focused trips, explore [Belize culture and history tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/belize/). The mere presence of the "Culture and History" interest does not mean every tour visits Xunantunich: check the list of destinations.

## Preparing for your excursion

Wear comfortable closed shoes: the archaeological site has stone surfaces and steps. Bring water, a hat and sunscreen for the open plazas. After rain, sections of the paths and stairs may be slippery.

As access involves crossing the Mopan River, independent visitors should check ferry operations and archaeological park regulations. Timetables, admission fees and restrictions can change. On our tours, tickets and a guided visit are included on the relevant day, so travelers can follow the agreed itinerary.

If traveling with children or preferring moderate exertion, discuss the walking pace and climbing tall steps in advance. **You do not need to reach the highest point to appreciate Maya history**: the plazas themselves offer much to explore.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Xunantunich

### Is the excursion included in both tour prices?

Yes. Both itineraries list a guided Xunantunich visit, admission tickets and lunch among that day's included services. Other excursions and extra expenses differ between the trips.

### Are Xunantunich and Tikal in the same country?

No. [Xunantunich](/belize/place/xunantunich/) is in Belize, while [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/) is in Guatemala. Both sites are included only on ["Best of Belize"](/belize/tour/best-of-belize/). That journey has a separate Guatemala day and border fees payable separately.

### When is Xunantunich visited?

On [day two of "Mainland / Island"](/belize/tour/belize-mainland-island-adventure/) or [day three of "Best of Belize"](/belize/tour/best-of-belize/). These are confirmed days of the itineraries. Visiting the archaeological site does not involve sleeping among the ruins.

### After Maya heritage, should you choose caves or the sea?

Both itineraries include outdoor activities followed by the Caribbean coast. ["Mainland / Island"](/belize/tour/belize-mainland-island-adventure/) includes tubing, a domestic flight and snorkeling at Hol Chan. ["Best of Belize"](/belize/tour/best-of-belize/) adds Tikal, then cave tubing, the zoo and a ferry to San Pedro. Base your choice on these differences, not simply on Xunantunich appearing in both programs.

## Excursion to Rio Frio Cave in Belize

[Rio Frio Cave](/belize/place/rio-frio-cave/) lies within the forested Mountain Pine Ridge area of western [Belize](/belize/). A river runs through this large natural cavern. Its broad entrance, rocky arches and natural light make an impressive sight even for people who have never visited a cave before.

Ada Tours includes the cave on the [full-day "Caracol, Rio Frio Cave and Rio On Pools" excursion](/belize/caracol/caracol-rio-frio-rio-on-pools/). This is a combined itinerary: first an ancient Maya city, then stops at the cave and natural pools. It gives travelers a chance to see archaeological sites and unusual inland Belizean landscapes in a single day.

## What is Rio Frio Cave like?

Rio Frio forms part of the cave complex in the [Mountain Pine Ridge](/belize/place/mountain-pine-ridge-forest-reserve/) reserve. Unlike narrow passages requiring special skills, its main chamber is known for large openings and a spacious vault. The river flows through limestone formations, creating a natural passage through the cave.

Caves were also important to the Maya civilization in Belize: they were associated with water and ideas of the underworld. However, the Ada Tours excursion does not promise a separate archaeological investigation of the cave, access to closed chambers or a demanding caving route.

Visitors concentrate on the geology itself: walls, boulders, the riverbed and the transition from lit to shaded areas. Conditions near the water can change during rainy periods, so the accessible route always depends on safety on the day.

## Combining the cave with the Maya city of Caracol

The main cultural attraction on the excursion is [Caracol](/belize/place/caracol/), an archaeological complex surrounded by tropical forest. You will walk through ancient courtyards and plazas, see a ball court and climb the tall Caana structure.

On the way back toward the lodge, the route passes natural landmarks in Mountain Pine Ridge. Rio Frio offers a striking change: after the Maya's stone architecture, you encounter shapes created by flowing water and bedrock.

The third stop is the [Rio On natural pools](/belize/place/rio-on-pools/), with time allocated for rest and swimming. Although the pools are part of the same excursion, do not assume that swimming is also automatically included at the cave.

## Excursion format and services

The [Caracol, Rio Frio and Rio On itinerary](/belize/caracol/caracol-rio-frio-rio-on-pools/) lasts **a full day** and is a guided excursion with an **English-speaking guide**.

Confirmed inclusions are the guided program and entrance tickets as specified. Personal expenses and services not stated in the program are extra. The published standalone excursion does not specify one fixed total price.

This is an important distinction: the cave page describes a stop on a combined route, but a separate cave admission ticket, independent transfer or dedicated personal guide is not offered as a standalone Ada Tours product here.

## Preparing for the visit

For a walk in the natural area, bring comfortable closed shoes with good grip, lightweight clothing for a warm humid climate, insect repellent and rain protection. Stones inside and around the cave can be wet and uneven. Safety matters more than speed: do not step onto slippery ledges for photographs.

The full-day journey through Caracol and Mountain Pine Ridge involves drives along forest roads. Confirm the length of individual stops before traveling so your expectations of the archaeological and nature sections match the schedule.

If the cave scenery is your main interest, read about [Rio Frio as a destination](/belize/place/rio-frio-cave/). To combine natural landscapes with Maya history, the full excursion is a better fit.

## Frequently asked questions about Rio Frio

### Can you visit Rio Frio without Caracol?

We offer a **combined full-day itinerary** with Caracol and the Rio On Pools. A standalone cave-only excursion is not listed here.

### Do you need special caving training?

The published description does not call for a specialist sporting expedition to visit the accessible part of the cave. However, the guide and local conditions determine the route and areas visitors may enter.

### What language is the excursion in?

The combined excursion has an **English-speaking guide**. Another language or a private format requires separate arrangements.

## Excursion to the Rio On natural pools in Belize

The [Rio On natural pools](/belize/place/rio-on-pools/) lie within Mountain Pine Ridge Forest Reserve. The river runs between wide slabs of granite, creating little waterfalls and basins of cool water. They are a natural stop on itineraries through western Belize, especially welcome after a visit to ancient Maya sites.

We include Rio On on the [full-day "Caracol, Rio Frio Cave and Rio On Pools" excursion](/belize/caracol/caracol-rio-frio-rio-on-pools/). Time for **relaxation and swimming** is part of the itinerary. No standalone excursion limited to the pools is listed in this catalog.

## Why the Rio On Pools are worth visiting

Rio On is unlike an ordinary beach: water flows over a rocky riverbed, with natural depressions between smooth granite surfaces creating several pools. Pine forest grows nearby, a surprising sight for travelers who associate Belize only with tropical coastline and coral reefs.

Granite surfaces warm in the sun, while the water temperature depends on the season, time of day and section of river. Open flat rocks are pleasant places to rest, but can be slippery beside the water. The strength of the current also changes after rain.

To learn about the surrounding landscape, see the [Mountain Pine Ridge](/belize/place/mountain-pine-ridge-forest-reserve/) page. The pools lie in this forested area and can readily be combined with its other natural attractions on the same trip.

## Swimming: what is planned and what to consider

Our itinerary allocates time at Rio On for relaxation and swimming. It is a chance to enjoy the water after the cultural part of the day, but not a promise that swimming will be possible in every season and under all river conditions.

A natural watercourse does not have the controlled conditions of a hotel pool. Before entering the water, assess the current, depth and rocks, and follow the guide's instructions. Heavy rain can change water levels and flow rates. Children and less confident swimmers need particular caution.

Bring swimwear, a change of clothes, a towel and non-slip shoes. The excursion description does not specify private changing cabins or equipment rental.

## The full itinerary via Caracol

The [Ada Tours excursion](/belize/caracol/caracol-rio-frio-rio-on-pools/) begins with the archaeological site of [Caracol](/belize/place/caracol/). Here travelers explore Maya structures, ancient courtyards, ball courts and the tall Caana pyramid.

On the return journey, the route stops at [Rio Frio Cave](/belize/place/rio-frio-cave/) and then the Rio On Pools. The itinerary returns to the lodge in the evening. One day combines ancient history with two contrasting natural landscapes: a limestone cave and a granite riverbed.

This is particularly convenient for travelers who want to see Caracol and also enjoy some time relaxing. Yet walking and swimming are parts of a combined excursion; the listing does not confirm a standalone transfer to Rio On from Belize City or elsewhere.

## Guide language, admission and other terms

On the [Caracol, Rio Frio and Rio On excursion](/belize/caracol/caracol-rio-frio-rio-on-pools/), you are accompanied by an **English-speaking guide**, and the trip lasts **a full day**.

Guided services and admission tickets are included as specified by the program. Personal expenses and services not listed are paid separately. The public listing does not give one fixed price for the standalone trip.

Before booking, agree on departure time, stop durations, the possibility of swimming in the season and return arrangements. Plans on forest roads and at the river may depend on rainfall.

## Including Rio On in a Belize journey

If your main interest is Maya culture, Rio On offers a natural continuation of a day at Caracol. If relaxing beside water is more important, remember that the confirmed excursion visits several places rather than allocating many hours to the pools.

For a trip through western Belize, allow extra time for travel and changeable weather. Find more options in the [Belize excursions catalog](/belize/excursion/), but check the specific itinerary before assuming Rio On is included in any other route.

## Frequently asked questions about Rio On Pools

### Can you swim in the Rio On Pools?

Swimming is part of the confirmed Ada Tours itinerary. Safe access to the water on a particular day depends on currents and weather.

### Can you combine Rio On with a cave visit?

Yes. The [Caracol–Rio Frio–Rio On itinerary](/belize/caracol/caracol-rio-frio-rio-on-pools/) includes both the cave and the river pools. It is one excursion product.

### Should you bring swimwear?

Yes, if you intend to take the opportunity to swim. A towel, dry change of clothes and shoes for rocky ground are also useful.

## From Maya ruins to the Caribbean: a 9-day itinerary

The **"Belize: Best of Both Worlds"** tour combines Maya heritage with time on the Caribbean Sea. The first **5 nights** are in San Ignacio, the base for excursions to the ancient city of [Caracol](/belize/place/caracol/), [Actun Tunichil Muknal Cave](/belize/place/actun-tunichil-muknal-cave/), [Barton Creek](/belize/place/barton-creek-cave/) and Tikal. Travelers then fly to [Ambergris Caye](/belize/place/ambergris-caye/) for **3 nights** in San Pedro.

Belize remains the main country on the itinerary, but **Tikal is in neighboring Guatemala** and is visited on a day excursion returning to Belize that evening. This is an important detail when choosing a trip: the international border crossing and possible border fees must be considered separately, as set out in the program.

Unlike a shorter [San Pedro beach holiday](/belize/tour/belize-san-pedro-ambergris-caye/), most of this journey is devoted to active excursions in western Belize. Relaxation on the island comes at the end of a busy cultural itinerary.

## First 5 nights: San Ignacio, Caracol and caves

After arriving at Belize's international airport, guests are transferred to San Ignacio and check in at San Ignacio Resort Hotel (Garden View).

On day two, travelers explore [Caracol](/belize/place/caracol/), a major Maya archaeological site in Belize's forest interior. Day three is devoted to [Actun Tunichil Muknal](/belize/place/actun-tunichil-muknal-cave/), often called ATM. This is very different from walking around a prepared museum: the cave itinerary may include wading, swimming and negotiating rocky passages. The excursion requires admission and a licensed local guide. Before booking, confirm physical demands, water conditions and entry restrictions.

Day four features a visit to [Barton Creek Cave](/belize/place/barton-creek-cave/), which introduces another aspect of the region's cave heritage. The two cave experiences are not interchangeable: their methods of access and levels of physical activity differ.

## A day in Guatemala: visiting Tikal

Day five includes a trip across the border to [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/), an archaeological complex in Guatemala. A guided tour, lunch and entrance tickets are planned. Afterward, travelers return to their hotel in San Ignacio.

This day lets visitors compare the archaeology of two countries without a separate multi-day tour of Guatemala. Crossing the border does, however, require checking travel documents, entry and exit times and fees. Consult the current requirements of both countries for your specific travel date.

## Final 3 nights: San Pedro and Ambergris Caye

On day six, travelers make an overland transfer from San Ignacio to the airfield in Belize City, followed by a domestic flight to San Pedro. On the island they stay at Ramon's Village. The next two days are free for relaxing or separately arranged optional excursions.

This is an opportunity for reef trips, exploring the island or simply resting after caves and transfers. However, additional marine activities **are not listed as mandatory paid excursions included in the tour**. They must be selected and arranged separately.

On day nine, a domestic flight takes travelers from San Pedro to Belize's international airport for their homeward flight.

## What's included and who will enjoy the tour?

The program includes accommodation at San Ignacio Resort Hotel and Ramon's Village, breakfasts, guided excursions to Caracol, ATM, Barton Creek and Tikal, plus lunches and admission tickets on the specified excursion days. Border fees, optional entertainment, personal purchases and other expenses named in the terms are extra.

The itinerary suits travelers who want to combine Maya archaeology, cave experiences and several days beside the sea. If demanding sections of ATM are unsuitable for your physical abilities, raise this before booking: the activity requires specific arrangements rather than simply being classified as an "easy excursion."

## Frequently asked questions about "Best of Both Worlds"

### Is Guatemala included in the journey?

Yes. There is a day trip to Tikal with a return to Belize. Belize is the main country for accommodation and the core itinerary.

### Is visiting ATM Cave difficult?

The visit involves moving through a natural cave and may include sections in water. Confirm participation requirements, permissions and guiding in advance.

### How much time is allocated to the beach?

The final **3 nights** are in San Pedro. Days 7–8 are free, and on day 9 travelers fly to the international airport.

### Are excursion entrance tickets included?

The listed services for Caracol, ATM, Barton Creek and Tikal include guided excursions, lunches and entrance tickets. Border fees are separate.

## Birdwatching in Belize: lagoons, forests and Tikal

This tour lasts **14 days and 13 nights**. Starting in [Belize City](/belize/place/belize-city/), the route crosses protected natural areas and Maya heritage sites in central and western Belize. It includes a **two-day program at [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/) in Guatemala** and ends with four nights on [Ambergris Caye](/belize/place/ambergris-caye/).

The distinguishing feature is the variety of habitats rather than one reserve. At the Crooked Tree lagoons, visitors look for waterbirds and shore-dwelling species. In the forests of Cockscomb Basin and Cayo, different birds and forest behaviors are the focus. A special observation stop is planned along the Hummingbird Highway. Time by the sea provides a more relaxed ending to the active route.

## Where birdwatching takes place on the itinerary

**[Crooked Tree](/belize/place/crooked-tree-wildlife-sanctuary/)** encompasses lagoons and wetlands. It is visited on day two together with the [Altun Ha archaeological site](/belize/place/altun-ha/). Here, look for birds around open water and shoreline vegetation. Belize's official tourism portal identifies the reserve as a major birdwatching destination. Sightings depend on water levels, season and the time of the visit.

**[Cockscomb Basin](/belize/place/cockscomb-basin-wildlife-sanctuary/)** occupies the whole of day four, devoted to a forest reserve. It is particularly famous for jaguar conservation, but the itinerary also describes trails and diverse birds. Visitors rarely see a jaguar, and the tour provides no such guarantee. A quiet pace, muted clothing and time to stop and listen are helpful on forest birdwatching walks.

On day six, while traveling from [Dangriga](/belize/place/dangriga/) to the [Cayo](/belize/place/cayo/) area, there is a stop on the Hummingbird Highway. This is observation along the journey, not another full day in a separate reserve. Counting only the listed locations would misrepresent the schedule: each stop has a different duration and habitat.

Other natural areas also feature in the middle and later parts of the route: [St. Herman's Cave](/belize/place/st-hermans-cave/), [St. Herman's Blue Hole National Park](/belize/place/st-hermans-blue-hole-national-park/) and forests around San Ignacio. These stops add to the country's natural diversity, although the cave day primarily focuses on the underground complex.

| Area | Main experience |
|---|---|
| Crooked Tree | Lagoons and waterbirds |
| Cockscomb Basin | Forest trails and wildlife |
| Hummingbird Highway | Birdwatching en route |
| Tikal | Archaeology among forests |
| Ambergris Caye | Reef and seaside relaxation |

## Two days at Tikal: an important border crossing

On day seven, a guided excursion begins at [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/), where ancient Maya buildings stand within tropical forest. Admission, lunch and an overnight stay at Jungle Lodge are planned. The morning of day eight is free for independent exploration, after which the group returns to [San Ignacio](/belize/place/san-ignacio/).

**Tikal is in Guatemala.** Belize is the main tour destination, but this two-day section involves an actual international border crossing. **Border fees are not included** in the program price. Visa and transit requirements must be checked individually according to nationality, travel documents and border crossings; they cannot be determined solely from the tour's name or hotel booking.

Day nine includes a visit to the [Belize Zoo](/belize/place/belize-zoo/) with lunch and an admission ticket. For nature enthusiasts, this is an opportunity to see local wildlife in a different setting, without relying on chance sightings on a forest trail.

## Final four nights on Ambergris Caye

After mainland excursions, the itinerary includes a transfer via Belize City and a boat to San Pedro. The next marine activity takes place around [Hol Chan Marine Reserve](/belize/place/hol-chan-marine-reserve/) and Shark Ray Alley: snorkeling among reef fish, rays and nurse sharks. This differs from land-based birdwatching and is subject to marine weather, water conditions and protected-area regulations.

The following island days are free for relaxation and possible additional activities. **Four nights at Sunbreeze Hotel** are scheduled. The hotel and return domestic transportation to the international airport appear among the included services. Optional excursions and personal expenses are listed separately.

Note the difference between two interests: the trip is indeed suitable for those who want to [watch birds and other wildlife](/interests/wildlife/tours/belize/), but the final portion also focuses on [Belize's Caribbean coast](/belize/) and marine experiences. This is a varied journey, not fourteen full days of specialist field birdwatching.

## What's included and how to prepare

Accommodation consists of **2 nights at Best Western Biltmore Plaza**, **3 nights at Pelican Beach Resort**, **1 night at Jungle Lodge**, **3 nights at Cahal Pech Village** and **4 nights at Sunbreeze Hotel**. Excursions, transfers, breakfasts and lunches are included as specified for each day; some time is set aside for independent relaxation. International flights, border fees, additional entertainment and tips are excluded.

For birdwatching, pack light binoculars, a rainproof bag, shoes for wet trails and clothing in subdued colors. These are personal equipment suggestions; **the tour does not confirm that such items are provided**. On the island, you will also need gear suitable for snorkeling and sun protection. When packing, account for forest walks, sea transfers and nights in different locations.

**When to travel:** do not assess the season using a single national rainfall average. At Crooked Tree, access to viewing areas and the presence of particular birds can change with water levels. Belize's official tourism portal identifies the roughly November–May dry season as an important birdwatching window in this reserve. Compare your dates with your main interests and check the forecast closer to departure.

## Who will enjoy this 14-day itinerary?

If your main goal is birdwatching in different natural environments, with archaeology and the sea as complementary interests, this route offers more nature stops than a brief introduction to the country. It also suits travelers who want to include [Maya sites](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/belize/) and neighboring Guatemala without arranging every transfer independently.

For a shorter trip with two free days by the sea, consider the [eight-day "Mainland / Island" itinerary](/belize/tour/belize-mainland-island-adventure/). Travelers interested in several seaside bases and an active cave day can compare the [13-day "Explore Belize" tour](/belize/tour/explore-belize/). All options are available in the [Belize tours catalog](/belize/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about birdwatching in Belize

### Can you see every bird species mentioned?

No. Sightings depend on season, time of day, weather and wildlife behavior. The itinerary provides visits to natural areas but cannot guarantee encounters with specific species.

### Are documents needed for Guatemala?

For the two-day Tikal excursion, entry to Guatemala and re-entry to Belize must be checked for each traveler's nationality. Border fees are not included in the base package.

### Is every day devoted only to birds?

No. The itinerary also includes visits to Maya sites, a cave day, transfers, snorkeling at sea and free time. The principal birdwatching stops are Crooked Tree, Cockscomb Basin and the Hummingbird Highway.

### Where does the journey end?

From San Pedro, travelers take a boat to Belize City and a road transfer to the international airport. International flights are an additional expense.
